newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks smash records as Wall St soars.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks smash records as Wall St soars.

text.p: Wall Street's bull run propelled European stocks to closing highs on Friday as worries faded over the outlook for Europe's single currency and helped prices higher.
Friday the 13th proved lucky for the Paris bourse in particular, which surged 48.25 points, or 1.75 percent, to close at a new high of 2,808.52, having traded as high as high as 2,811.86.
Paris shares led the charge higher throughout the day and received a late boost after comments emerging from a Franco-German summit on the euro.

One broker said although the meeting between President Jacques Chirac and Chancellor Helmut Kohl yielded no dramatic fresh factors, the comments showed "there was progress on the way to an agreement on the stability pact".
EU leaders convene for a summit in Amsterdam on Monday, where the final review of the Maastricht Treaty on EMU and post-EMU budgetary stability pact are expected to be agreed.

Last-minute jitters about the success of the summit and the timetable for the single currency have been raised since the newly-elected Socialist government in France has insisted on the inclusion of a more pro-employment bias to the stability pact which is designed to ensure budgetry discipline after the euro is introduced in 1999.
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and his Finance Minister Theo Waigel met French President Jacques Chirac, his Prime Minister Lional Jospin and French Finance Minister Dominque Strauss-Kahn.
Their comments all pointed to progress on an agreement at or before Monday's EU summit but that further work was needed. All said they wanted EMU on time in 1999.
Waigel said, "We hope we will be able to find a solution."

Germany's 30-share DAX index also ended bourse trade at a record close, up 36.45 points, or around one percent, at 3,744.44 points after earlier reaching a new trading high of 3,762.58 points. It, too, benefited from the easing of fears about the future of European monetary union.

"There is more and more confidence out there that the euro will come on time, even if it's weaker than expected, so people now expect that money will keep coming into Europe after currency union," a German share trader said.
But it was Wall Street's rampant surge which again proved the decisive factor for Europe's bourses.
The Dow Jones industrial index of leading U.S. shares was up 56.54 points at 7,768.01, or 0.7 percent, at the close of European business, having hit no less than five closing highs in a row.
Wall Street's seemingly unstoppable bullishness pushed London's FTSE 100 index to its third record close this week, though domestic bid activity also helped boost investor confidence.
The FTSE 100 index finished up 25.7 points, or 0.5 percent, at 4,783.1 but off the day's best levels after an unsuccessful early attempt to jump the 4,800 barrier, chalking up a best of 4,796.0.
"It has been quite a testing day," said one trader. "The higher the market goes the more amazed we become. Wall St bubbled off its best but is still beyond the rules of gravity."

The catalyst behind the Wall Street's latest move was data showing U.S. producer prices fell 0.3 percent in May, their fifth straight decline and making the first time the index has dropped five months in succession since 1952.

"This is very positive news on inflation which will probably be backed up (U.S.) consumer price figures next Tuesday," said Rob Hayward, economist at Bank of America in London, interviewed on Reuters Financial Television.
Share traders on both sides of the Atlantic are driving shares higher in the belief that the U.S. is enjoying a rare period of inflation free gwowth.

The dollar rallied more than one pfennig and half a yen in Europe on the back of a another robust rise in U.S. stocks and bonds and amid more positive sign of a Franco-German accord on the details of European monetary union.
Comments from the Franco-German summit in France, meantime, raised hopes of an imminent agreement on the final nuances of the post-EMU stability pact and kept traders wary of marks.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7370 marks and 114.70 yen compared with 1.7265 marks and 113.99 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index finished was up 25.7 points at 4,783.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed was up 48.25 points at 2,808.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 36.45 points at 3,744.44.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1530 GMT
Gold closed at $341.55 with $342.65 an ounce in late trade on Thursday.
